target_customer: Individual and small-business online sellers on eBay, Amazon and Overstock
problem: Sellers had to list and manage items across several marketplaces by hand and lacked a central inventory view or tools to optimize sales.
business_model: SaaS tool for marketplace sellers (pricing not found)
product_category: Multi-marketplace seller inventory and listing tools

founders.name: Kulveer Taggar
education: University of Oxford (per Wikipedia on Patrick Collison, 'Oxford graduates')
founders.background_notes: Named as founder in Live Current announcement coverage; later press says he founded Auctomatic during college.

founders.name: Harjeet Taggar
education: University of Oxford (per Wikipedia on Patrick Collison, 'Oxford graduates')
founders.background_notes: Brother of Kulveer; later a YC partner (not verified in this run).

founders.name: Patrick Collison
founders.background_notes: Per Wikipedia, Collison brothers' Limerick startup Shuppa merged with the Taggars to form Auctomatic after YC interest; John Collison's role not confirmed by the sources read.

competitors.name: Vendio
competitors.what: Third-party eBay seller management service; Auctomatic imported inventory from it

competitors.name: Marketworks
competitors.what: Third-party eBay seller management service; Auctomatic imported inventory from it

competitors.name: ChannelAdvisor
competitors.what: Multi-channel marketplace listing and inventory service; Auctomatic imported inventory from it

technical_complexity.rationale: Syncing inventory, listings and sales with eBay and other marketplace APIs, plus CSV import and image hosting, is standard engineering with integration pain; the beta in Oct 2007 shipped about 9 months after the Winter 2007 batch started.

defensibility.rationale: Inventory and templates stored in the tool create mild lock-in, but the features (one-page form, reusable templates, sync) were copyable and incumbents such as Vendio and Marketworks already served sellers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying it; instead Communicate.com (Live Current Media) bought it in March 2008 for $5M in cash and stock and required the founders to move to Vancouver.

market_need_then: eBay and multi-marketplace selling was large by 2007, and a cottage industry of third-party listing and management services (Vendio, Marketworks, ChannelAdvisor) existed, showing sellers paid for tooling; no direct usage figures for Auctomatic were found.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Mashable and TechCrunch at launch and sale; no sign of fan community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive coinage (auction plus -omatic) that conveys the function, but one video summary even garbled it as 'Octomatic'; no mascot, community or brand press found, and the brand disappeared inside Live Current Media within a year.

outcome_analysis: Auctomatic was a two-to-three person Winter 2007 team, partly the Collison brothers' Shuppa merged with the Taggar brothers, that shipped a multi-marketplace seller inventory beta in October 2007 and sold to Communicate.com (Live Current Media) for about $5M in cash and stock in March 2008, roughly a year after founding. The wedge was copyable and sat among established seller-tool vendors, so a quick strategic sale to a domain-and-web company that wanted to move into products looks like a modest, soft-landing-style exit; the price is press-reported and the product did not continue as an independent business.
notes: Price $5M cash and stock from TechCrunch; the company announcement itself said terms undisclosed (per Chief Marketer) and Seedtable also lists $5M. Funding: TechCrunch names backers Y Combinator, Paul Buchheit and Chris Sacca; no amounts found, so no rounds recorded. Competitors are tools Auctomatic imported from (named in an Oct 2007 launch write-up that reprints Mashable); direct competitive positioning is not stated. Wikipedia 'Auctomatic' redirects into the Patrick Collison article; founders list combines that article and search coverage of the Live Current announcement; John Collison involvement unverified. Founders' prior employers unknown. Web Archive skipped.
